desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list is passed to your function as an array holding the node values from head to tail; an empty array is an empty list. You may build real nodes from it first, or work on the array directly. The result is also returned as an array of values from head to tail.

Cut the list into consecutive groups whose intended sizes are 1, 2, 3, 4, ... (the first group has 1 node, the second 2 nodes, the third 3 nodes, and so on). The last group takes whatever is left, so its real size may be smaller than its intended size.

Reverse every group whose real size is even, and leave groups of odd size unchanged. Return the resulting list. For example [5,2,6,3,9,1,7,3,8,4] splits into [5] [2,6] [3,9,1] [7,3,8,4]; the groups of sizes 2 and 4 are reversed, giving [5,6,2,3,9,1,4,8,3,7]. And [1,1,0,6] splits into [1] [1,0] [6] (the last group wanted 3 nodes but only 1 is left) and gives [1,0,1,6].
hints: The group boundaries are determined by position only, so you can find them while walking: group number g starts right after the previous one and wants g nodes.
For each group, first count how many nodes it really has (at most g, fewer at the end of the list). Then decide: reverse if that real count is even.

Keep a pointer prev to the node just before the group. To reverse cnt nodes in place, take the group's first node as the future tail and repeatedly move the node after the tail to the front of the group, cnt - 1 times. Afterwards the tail is the new prev; if you did not reverse, just advance prev by cnt nodes.
editorial: Walk with a pointer prev that stands right before the current group and a variable size = 1, 2, 3, ... For each group count the real number of nodes cnt = min(size, remaining) by stepping ahead from prev.next. If cnt is odd, simply move prev forward by cnt nodes.

If cnt is even, reverse the group in place: the first node of the group, tail, will end up last. Do cnt - 1 times: nxt = tail.next; tail.next = nxt.next; nxt.next = prev.next; prev.next = nxt, which moves the node after the tail to the front of the group. Then set prev = tail. Every node is counted once and relinked at most once, so the time is O(n) with O(1) extra space. The only subtle point is the last group: its parity depends on how many nodes are really there, not on the intended size.
